Head_and_Face: Large prominent compound eyes occupy a significant portion of the head.
Large sickle-shaped mandibles are visible at the anterior.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is elongated and streamlined with hardened elytra.
Elytra display bright metallic coloration (iridescent green, bronze, or blue).
Distinctive white or cream-colored curvilinear markings are present on the elytra surface.
Thorax is elongated relative to the abdomen.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long, slender, and adapted for rapid running.
Six-jointed legs with tarsal claws for gripping surfaces.
Filiform antennae are segmented and mobile.

Head_and_Face: Antennae are short and clubbed.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact, hemispherical, and dome-shaped with smooth glossy elytra.
Coloration is bright and saturated (red, orange, or yellow) with distinct circular black spots distributed symmetrically across the elytra.
Pronotum is black with characteristic white lateral markings.
Width is nearly equal to length, creating a rounded silhouette.
Body surface is highly reflective with a polished appearance.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are relatively short and tucked beneath the body.
Six legs with small tarsal segments.

Head_and_Face: Prominent forward-projecting mandibles are visible.
Antennae are filiform, thread-like, and segmented.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is flattened and elongated-oval with hard elytra.
Elytra display iridescent black or metallic bronze coloration.
Parallel longitudinal striations (grooves) run along the entire elytra surface.
Body surface has a glossy sheen.
Thorax is slightly narrower than the abdomen.
Coloration is dark and uniform with metallic reflections under light.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long and cursorial with spiny tibiae.
Six legs with well-developed femora.

Head_and_Face: Robust chewing mandibles are visible.
Antennae are extremely long, filiform, and extend beyond body length (1.5-2x body length).
Antennae are composed of numerous distinct segments.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is elongated and cylindrical with hardened elytra.
Coloration patterns include mottled browns, blacks, or banded patterns on the elytra.
Body surface texture ranges from smooth to punctate.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are moderately long with tarsal claws for gripping bark.
Six legs with segmented structure.

Head_and_Face: Antennae are short to moderate in length.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is oval to broadly rounded with smooth elytra.
Elytra display bright aposematic coloration (yellow, green, orange, or metallic hues).
Contrasting dark markings or bands are often present on the elytra.
Body surface may be smooth or finely punctate.
Body width is substantial relative to length, creating a broad oval silhouette.
Coloration often mimics host plant leaves.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are relatively short with tarsal segments adapted for clinging to foliage.
Six legs with adhesive capabilities.

Head_and_Face: Antennal clubs are lamellate and plate-like.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust, compact, and ovoid with hard glossy elytra.
Coloration is dark (black or dark brown).
Body surface has a smooth polished appearance.
Body is compact with disproportionately large forelegs.
Coloration is dark and uniform with a subtle metallic sheen.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Forelegs are flattened and spiny, adapted for digging.
Legs are robust with prominent spines on tibiae.
Six legs with specialized digging adaptations.

Head_and_Face: Prominent cephalic horn(s) project anteriorly from the head.
Secondary thoracic horn is often present.
Horn surface is smooth and curved upward or forward.
Antennal clubs are lamellate.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is large, robust, and heavily-built with hard elytra.
Coloration is dark brown or black.
Body surface has a matte to semi-glossy finish.
Overall appearance is heavily armored.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are robust with tibial spines.
Six thick legs with strong gripping capability.

Head_and_Face: Distinctive elongated snout (rostrum) projects anteriorly from the head.
Antennae are elbowed (geniculate) and arise from the rostrum.
Rostrum length is often one-third to one-half of body length.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is small and compact.
Elytra have a textured surface including punctures, scales, or setae.
Coloration is typically cryptic (browns, grays, blacks) with mottled or banded patterns.
Body surface is often covered with fine scales or hairs providing camouflage.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are relatively short.
Six legs with tarsal claws.

Head_and_Face: Large prominent compound eyes occupy the majority of the head surface.
Antennae are short with an aristate bristle-like terminal segment.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact.
Single pair of membranous forewings with visible venation patterns.
Reduced hindwings are modified into small knobbed halteres visible laterally.
Body surface is variable: may be hairy, glossy, or matte.
Wingspan is typically 1.5-2x body length.
Wings are transparent with dark venation.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are slender with pulvilli adhesive pads on tarsi.
Six legs with specialized landing adaptations.

Head_and_Face: Antennae are elbowed.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and densely hairy (pubescent).
Characteristic black and yellow or white banding patterns are present on the abdomen.
Two pairs of membranous wings with visible venation; forewings are larger than hindwings.
Wings are often folded longitudinally at rest.
Body hairs are branched and plumose.
Body is robust and laterally compressed.
Wings extend beyond the abdomen when folded.
Stinger is visible at the posterior abdomen in females.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Hind legs have specialized pollen baskets (corbiculae) - smooth concave surfaces surrounded by hairs.
Six legs with pollen-carrying adaptations.
